thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] INC-2026-0042 — Region az1a — elevated TX sched latency observed on inference fleet. p99 token latency +120%, 502 errors spike. Auto-escalating to oncall.

alice (oncall): ack. I'm looking at metrics — seeing kernel tx-queue depth rising on a subset of g5 instances. Not a full AZ outage but hitting inference pods.

ben (infra): grabbing host logs now. attaching quick scrub: ```sudo dmesg | tail -n 50``` shows a few netdev TX timeouts and skb drops. Also seeing qdisc backlog growth on ens5.````

carol (runtime): confirm seeing KVCACHE stalls and retries correlating with the network jitter window — requests are timing out waiting for KV from peers. Rolling fallback to local cache helps temporarily.

alice (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) split traffic away from az1a to eu-west-1 and us-west-2 by adjusting routing policy (canary 30% az1a -> 70% remote). 2) reduce batch sizes for affected routes to reduce head-of-line blocking. 3) raise DNS TTL? no, lowering helps reroute faster — set to 30s.

ben (infra): starting traffic shift. patch to router policy: ```PATCH /routing/policy/az1a { weight: 0.3 -> 0.1 }``` executing now. edgebot: please confirm.

edgebot: traffic-split job queued. applied weights: az1a=0.12, eu-west-1=0.58, usw2=0.30. propagation ~15s. :white_check_mark:

carol (runtime): runtime flag flip to reduce default batch size: `--max-batch=8` -> `--max-batch=4` for route /v1/generate. Applying to service group A via canary (10% then 100%).

ben (infra): on hosts, doing a soft NIC reset on the worst offenders (`sudo ethtool -r ens5`) and clearing tx queues. Observed immediate drop in tx_pending on three hosts. Will keep draining if instability persists.

dan (support): we've had three customers report increased latency and a couple 502s (tickets #3421, #3424, #3426). I've queued a proactive message to customers on the status page with current mitigation steps.

alice (oncall): note — we're not seeing ENI attach limits or AZ-wide control-plane errors. This looks like kernel-level TX scheduling issue on some AMI/kernel combo. Ben — are those hosts all on the same kernel/AMI?

ben (infra): yes, they were on the last nightly AMI (ami-20260210). I see a pattern: hosts launched in the last 36h show the highest tx_lat. Rolling them back to previous AMI seems risky at scale. Prefer to evict and reprovision affected instances into a different AMI batch.

carol (runtime): as longer-term safety, I'm enabling the model fallback policy for premium customers only (downgrade to rtx-7b-quant when p95 latency > 2s). This is live for the next 30m window.

alice (oncall): ben, can you start streaming a filtered syslog and include `net/tx` counters to #eng-runtime-debug so they can correlate?

ben (infra): streaming to #eng-runtime-debug now. Command: ```journalctl -f -u network.service | grep -E "tx_queue|tx_timeout|skbs"```

edgebot: DNS TTL lowered for api.redwood.example -> 30s. New DNS propagation should push clients to alternate endpoints in <1m.

dan (support): posted update on status.redwood.com: "We are investigating increased latency and error rates impacting some inference requests in az1a. Traffic is being shifted and mitigations are underway."

alice (oncall): Okay we have metrics: after traffic shift and batch reduction p99 token latency down from +120% -> +18% and 502s trending down. But a small set of customers still hit degraded path when routed to az1a sticky sessions. We should clear sticky sessions for affected customers.

carol (runtime): running `POST /v1/sessions/clear?az=az1a&tag=sticky` for sticky session eviction. Doing in 2 waves.

ben (infra): continuing to cordon and reboot 6 nodes showing persistent tx_saturation. Provisioning replacements in az1b to keep capacity steady.

eli (oncall-backup): I'm coming on shift in 10m for formal handoff. alice, any blockers to hand off?

alice (oncall): main open items: 1) continue host reprovisioning; 2) monitor KV cache regen; 3) validate customer tickets cleared. Everything else under control. I'll hand off to you after next status update.

dan (support): tickets updated and customers on p1 list informed of mitigations. One customer requested SLA credit — flagged to sales.

ben (infra): host reprovisioning done for 4/6. Early reprovisions show healthy tx metrics with older AMI. Still waiting on two reboots.

carol (runtime): KV cache warmup completed for most pods; retries dropped to baseline. Monitoring dashboards show stable request success rates.

alice (oncall): last check: overall request error rate back to baseline, global p99 close to normal; az1a still slightly elevated but within warning thresholds. I'll hand off to eli now. :wave:

eli (oncall-backup): acked. Thanks alice — I'll keep watch and follow up if any of the reprovisioned hosts regress. Please paste any remaining host IDs and AMI diffs to #eng-infra after this thread.

alice (oncall): posted host list and AMI diff to #eng-infra. Summary I'll add to incident log: root cause suspected kernel/AMI-level TX scheduling regression on newly launched hosts in az1a leading to queuing and KV cache stalls. Mitigations: traffic split, batch reduction, DNS TTL reduction, host reprovisioning to stable AMI, session eviction, model fallback for sensitive customers.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0042 status -> monitoring. No longer paging.

edgebot: closing traffic emergency runbook entries and capturing timeline. :spiral_note_pad:

alice (oncall): closing thread — leaving notes for postmortem. Good coordination.

eli (oncall-backup): closing ack. Will open a follow-up postmortem PR with infra and runtime details.

carol (runtime): :thumbsup: will include KV cache timelines and graphs."
